terms.name: Accent color
terms.definition: The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.

terms.name: Additive colour
terms.definition: Colour made by adding light, where red, green and blue at full strength give white, which is why a screen is at its brightest when it is showing all three.

terms.name: App shortcut
terms.definition: A short menu of app actions hung off the app icon itself, opened by a long press or a secondary click before the app is even running.

terms.name: Autofill
terms.definition: The browser filling a form from values it has already saved, on its own or from a dropdown of the reader's own profile, so a field arrives answered.

terms.name: Bottom navigation
terms.definition: A bar of three to five top level destinations pinned to the bottom edge of a phone screen, with the current destination always marked.

terms.name: Button versus link
terms.definition: The rule that decides which element to use: a link goes somewhere, a button does something, and the choice sets the keyboard, the cursor, and the announced role.

terms.name: Character counter
terms.definition: The running count beside a text box showing how many characters are used, or how many remain, against a limit.

terms.name: Cloning
terms.definition: Spawning a new element visibly out of an existing one so the reader can see where it came from, rather than having it arrive from nowhere.

terms.name: Color scheme
terms.definition: The declaration that a page or element supports light or dark rendering, which also tells the browser which palette to use for scrollbars and form controls.

terms.name: Complementary colors
terms.definition: Two hues sitting opposite each other on the colour wheel, the pairing that produces the strongest contrast and the loudest accent.

terms.name: Content choreography
terms.definition: Deciding how blocks of content reorder and regroup as a layout reflows, so hierarchy survives the collapse from several columns into one.

terms.name: currentColor
terms.definition: A CSS keyword meaning the element's own text colour, letting borders, icons and fills inherit whatever colour the surrounding text happens to be.

terms.name: Decorative image
terms.definition: An image that carries no information and is given an empty alt attribute so assistive technology skips it entirely.

terms.name: Disclosure triangle
terms.definition: The small triangle beside a tree item that points right when collapsed and down when open, rotating as it toggles.

terms.name: Drag to create
terms.definition: Making a new object by dragging out its extent rather than pressing Add: an event drawn across two hours, a frame drawn on a canvas, a range drawn on a chart.

terms.name: Edge routing
terms.definition: How a connector gets from one node to another: a bezier sweep, a right-angled staircase, or a straight line, picked so the crossings stay readable.

terms.name: Error page
terms.definition: The whole screen a site serves instead of the page that was asked for: what happened, in the reader's words, and the shortest way back to something that works.

terms.name: Fallback font
terms.definition: The typeface actually used when the preferred one is missing or has not loaded, either for the whole run of text or for characters it lacks.

terms.name: Fitts's law
terms.definition: The rule that the time to hit a target grows with its distance and shrinks with its size, which is why screen edges and corners are so easy to reach.

terms.name: Focus follows mouse
terms.definition: A focus model in which whatever the pointer is over receives keyboard input, without any click to claim it first.

terms.name: Force touch
terms.definition: A press whose depth is part of the input, letting a harder press mean something different from a light one on a pressure sensing surface.

terms.name: Glassmorphism
terms.definition: A style where surfaces are translucent and blur what is behind them, separated from the backdrop by a hairline edge and a soft shadow.

terms.name: Gutenberg diagram
terms.definition: A model splitting evenly weighted pages into four quadrants, with the eye falling from the primary area at top left to the terminal area at bottom right.

terms.name: Hidden but focusable
terms.definition: An element hidden from assistive technology that is still in the tab sequence, so keyboard focus lands on something a screen reader refuses to describe.

terms.name: Hydration
terms.definition: The pass where script attaches behaviour to server-rendered HTML, turning a page that is already painted and readable into one that answers input.

terms.name: Ink trap
terms.definition: A notch cut out of a letter's inside corners so spreading ink or blurring pixels do not fill the joint solid.

terms.name: Invoker command
terms.definition: A button that names the element it acts on and what to do to it, in markup, so opening a dialog or toggling a popover needs no script at all.

terms.name: Keyframe
terms.definition: A point in an animation where a value is pinned, with the frames between generated by interpolating from one pinned point to the next.

terms.name: Lazy registration
terms.definition: Letting someone use a product and accumulate state anonymously, and asking for an account only when that state needs to survive the session.

terms.name: List
terms.definition: A vertical run of related items presented as a set, where the shared shape of every row is what tells a reader the rows belong together.

terms.name: Magic tap
terms.definition: A screen reader gesture that fires the one action a screen is most likely about, so the reader does not have to hunt for the control.

terms.name: Menu button
terms.definition: A button whose only job is to open a menu, marked with aria-haspopup and usually drawn with a downward chevron.

terms.name: Modal dialog
terms.definition: A window that opens over the page and takes control of it, so nothing behind can be used until the dialog is answered or dismissed.

terms.name: Multi select
terms.definition: A select that accepts several values at once, usually showing the chosen ones as removable tokens inside the field.

terms.name: New Wave design
terms.definition: The postmodern break from Swiss order: stair-stepped rules, diagonal and letter-spaced type, weights mixed inside a word, and text reversed out of bars.

terms.name: One thing per page
terms.definition: Asking a single question on each screen of a form so the reader never chooses which field to answer first and errors point somewhere unambiguous.

terms.name: Overloaded command
terms.definition: One command word or icon wired to different outcomes depending on where it sits, so having used it once teaches the reader nothing about the next one.

terms.name: Parenting
terms.definition: Tying one element's motion to another's so moving or scaling the parent carries the child with it, which is how a group of parts reads as one object instead of several.

terms.name: Playhead
terms.definition: The marker showing the current position in a timeline or track, which travels during playback and can be dragged to move it.

terms.name: Press-drag-release
terms.definition: Operating a menu in one gesture: pressing the trigger opens it, dragging moves through the items while the button stays down, and releasing over an item commits it.

terms.name: Prototype
terms.definition: A design wired up just enough to be tried: screens linked so that a tap goes somewhere, with nothing real behind the links.

terms.name: Range select
terms.definition: Choosing a contiguous run of items by marking one end and holding Shift while marking the other, selecting everything between them.

terms.name: Relative luminance
terms.definition: The brightness of a colour measured on a 0 to 1 scale after each channel is linearised, which is the input every WCAG contrast calculation actually uses.

terms.name: Role description
terms.definition: An author supplied name for a widget's role, spoken in place of the stock role name, which overrides the platform wording and misleads easily.

terms.name: Screen curtain
terms.definition: A screen reader mode that switches the display off entirely while navigation keeps working, used for privacy and by sighted testers checking an audio-only run.

terms.name: Scrubbing
terms.definition: Dragging a playhead along a timeline to move through media by hand, previewing frames as the position changes rather than waiting for playback.

terms.name: Serif
terms.definition: The small finishing stroke at the end of a letter's stem, and by extension the class of typefaces that have them.

terms.name: Skip link
terms.definition: A link at the very start of a page, revealed on focus, that jumps past repeated navigation to the main content.

terms.name: Solarpunk
terms.definition: An optimistic ecological future style of daylight palettes, plant growth over structure, stained glass colour, art nouveau curves, and visible solar and wind technology.

terms.name: Spotlight hover
terms.definition: A soft radial glow centred on the pointer's position inside a card, lighting its surface and border as the cursor moves and going dark when the cursor leaves.

terms.name: Stepped animation
terms.definition: Motion that jumps between a fixed number of discrete positions instead of interpolating, the mechanic behind sprite sheets, ticking clock hands and segmented spinners.

terms.name: Superfamily
terms.definition: A type system whose serif, sans, and sometimes mono members share one skeleton, so they pair by construction rather than by taste.

terms.name: System font
terms.definition: The typeface the operating system uses for its own interface, requested by keyword so each platform supplies its native face.

terms.name: Text field
terms.definition: A single line box for typed input, carrying a label, an optional hint, and the error message shown when what was typed does not pass.

terms.name: Tofu
terms.definition: The empty rectangle a font renders when it has no glyph for a character, named for the block of bean curd it resembles.

terms.name: Tree view
terms.definition: A nested list where branches expand and collapse in place, navigated with arrow keys as a single tab stop.

terms.name: Universal navigation
terms.definition: A slim bar that links a subsite back to its parent organisation's other sites, sitting above the subsite's own global navigation.

terms.name: Viewport
terms.definition: The visible rectangle of a page inside the browser window, excluding the browser's own bars, and the unit basis for vh and vw.

terms.name: Wipe
terms.definition: A transition where a moving edge or mask travels across the frame, replacing what was there with what comes next.
